seed_variation.verdict: Only one seed was run, so there is no seed variation to measure.
seed_variation.why: A hosted LLM cannot be seeded: our seeds only reach local random generators, and the provider's sampling (temperature etc.) is fixed for this model. So every run can give different text, and the spread across seeds measures the model's own run-to-run variation. Each seed repeats every API call. Each seed sets Python random, NumPy and torch. PYTHONHASHSEED is fixed to the FIRST seed for the whole run.

predictions.SY0103a: The team held a kick-off meeting for a new voice-controlled kitchen timer project, discussing retail pricing, profit goals, and local speech recognition. They agreed on using a distinct wake word, included a single physical button as a backup, and left the power options open pending component research. Finally, before concluding the meeting, the project manager assigned action items for components, voice commands, market research, and naming ideas.
predictions.SY0103b: The team chose Kiko as the working name and planned testing for kitchen phrases, while parking the two-digit display and power source questions pending Tomasz's input and cost numbers. The meeting concluded with assigning tasks for command lists, keyword testing, and competitor pricing research, while the project manager took over emailing Tomasz regarding the timer setup, chip capacity, cost breakdown, and power question.
predictions.SY0103c: The project manager reviewed component costs, which stand at eleven thirty per unit with an added LED display, remaining within the budget limit. The team discussed the final command structure, wake word tuning, and competitor analysis supporting a twenty-five euro price point. The industrial designer introduced a palm-sized round puck design featuring a wipeable plastic shell and a soft rubber top button integrating the display. After discussing magnets and colour options for the device, the meeting concluded with assigned tasks for the next session.
predictions.SY0103d: The project manager opened the final detailed design meeting by confirming the wake word fix and presenting the physical model. The industrial designer explained the hardware layout, and Priya presented the display and timer logic. After discussing casing colors to avoid a medical device look, the team agreed on two colorways paired with a white LED display, keeping unit costs under the target. Finally, the team evaluated their design goals, confirming hands-free voice control, an elbow-friendly button, an eighty-five decibel ramping alarm, and a competitive twenty-five dollar price point driven by offline capability without wifi. The project manager reviewed the action items before concluding the meeting.
predictions.SY0110a: Project manager Priya opened the kickoff meeting with industrial designer Tom and user interface designer Jonas to discuss designing a reusable coffee cup and deposit system, establishing targets like a one euro deposit, production costs under three euros, and fifty partner cafes in the first year. The team explored design ideas and return methods, agreeing that the cups must be dishwasher-safe and compatible with standard cafe lid sizes. They also planned to consult Marta, who returns on Thursday, about cafe owner perspectives and discussed leaving the issue of lost cups open for further consideration. Finally, they scheduled the next functional design meeting for shortly after.
predictions.SY0110b: The project manager reviewed the decisions made so far, confirming polypropylene cups with a ninety-millimetre rim, counter returns at partner cafes without machines, and a week-long dishwasher test at Cafe Lindner. They wrapped up the session by assigning action items and scheduling the conceptual design meeting for the same time next week.
predictions.SY0110c: The project manager reviewed dishwasher tests from Cafe Lindner, confirming durability while switching to in-mould labelling after the logo faded, and the team approved adding a ribbed band for grip. The meeting then addressed sizing, deciding to stick with a single three hundred millilitre size for launch to maintain the ninety millimetre rim standard for lids. Regarding aesthetics, the team agreed on a slate grey base colour to ensure brand recognition and hide stains across cafes. The user interface designer presented the counter return flow, establishing that customers can swap dirty cups for clean ones or receive their euro deposit back without staff arguing over damaged items. Finally, the user interface designer showed the slate grey window badge, and the team discussed the increased loss cost per cup, leading the project manager to agree to raise the absorption of lost cup costs with management. Marta agreed to write the staff guide and check the slate grey colour with Mr Lindner.
predictions.SY0110d: The project manager opened the final detailed design meeting, noting Jonas's absence despite his completed badge design. Industrial Designer reported pricing for ten thousand units and a mould fee, which were agreed upon, while management approved covering cup losses via a monthly partner fee. Marketing Expert presented the laminated staff guide and reported Café Lindner's approval of the slate grey colour. The team approved embossing the return value on the base and rejected a second launch colour. The team reviewed lead times, and Project Manager agreed to contact Jonas about the print file while Industrial Designer will confirm the production order. Finally, Project Manager agreed to write the final management report and the meeting minutes to conclude the session.
predictions.SY0202a: Marcus opened the kickoff meeting for the library self-checkout kiosk project with a budget under four thousand euros and a sale price of six and a half thousand euros. The team agreed that the kiosk should handle checkouts and renewals, use a single scanner for cards and QR codes, and address accessibility requirements. Toward the end, Marcus assigned preparation tasks for the upcoming functional design meeting: Tomas will map out internal components and rough layout, Hannah will outline the checkout and renewal user flow, Priya will gather user and library requirements, and Marcus will circulate the project brief and today's meeting notes.
predictions.SY0202b: The team reviewed the library kiosk design, estimating total costs and incorporating feedback on accessibility, email receipts, and hardware adjustments. The project manager assigned Hannah to update the checkout and renewal flow, while Priya agreed to check RFID pricing with an existing supplier and Tomas took on preparing casing sketches incorporating the new heights. Finally, the project manager agreed to circulate the meeting notes and brief Hannah on the physical help button before concluding the session.
predictions.SY0202c: The team reviewed RFID pricing and noted that four branches still use barcodes, prompting a plan to include an RFID reader pad and a barcode scanner fallback. Industrial Designer presented three casing sketches, and the group selected the desk-like shape with a tilted screen, opting for oak veneer and aluminium edging to reach around three thousand two hundred and seventy euros. User Interface Designer then presented the revised user flow, covering card or app login, simultaneous RFID stacking, barcode fallback, simple renewals, preselected email receipts, and a help button with a long-press audio mode. After discussing text-to-speech engine options tied to the embedded hardware, the team agreed Industrial Designer will handle the PC and speech engine selection, while keeping the fifteen-inch screen size for now. Finally, the project manager assigned action items for the upcoming detailed design session and agreed to circulate the updated cost breakdown.
predictions.SY0202d: The team agreed to use the licensed text-to-speech board, reviewed Hannah's screen layouts, and heard Priya's high evaluation scores. The project manager then calculated total unit costs at three thousand four hundred and ten euros, leaving ample headroom and prompting Priya to assign a score for cost. They rejected an LED ring for the help button to keep the design simple. Finally, the project manager reviewed action items and set deadlines before concluding the meeting.
predictions.SY0209a: Laura opened the kickoff meeting for a new protective case for the Learnly seven-inch children's educational tablet, establishing that the project focuses on this specific device and maintaining the four-to-eight target age group. Laura outlined the financial constraints of a twenty-five Euro selling price and a twelve-fifty production cost limit. The team brainstormed features, agreeing on drop protection using rubber or foam with thick corners, a carrying handle, and a raised lip around the screen instead of a fragile flap. They also discussed wipeable materials, considered market pricing, and briefly touched on a name tag window before parking the idea. Finally, tasks were assigned for user research, functional design, drop testing standards, and material budgeting, and Laura concluded the meeting.
predictions.SY0209b: The team targeted a one point two metre drop height, chose EVA foam with thick corners, and opted for a fixed handle, a raised screen lip, covered buttons, and an open charging port. They also decided to wait for survey results on the name tag window, dropped swappable covers, and reassigned the retail price check to Tomasz. Finally, the project manager assigned Priya to sketch the fixed handle and cut-outs, asked Ben to get a supplier quote for the case, and scheduled colour discussions for the next meeting.
predictions.SY0209c: The team reviewed survey results confirming a preference for dark or bright colours, durable foam, handles, and name tags, and decided to launch with strong blue and lime green while dropping the idea of a stylus slot. The Industrial Designer reported a total unit cost of nine euro thirty before the name tag window, which fits comfortably within the budget. For the upcoming detailed design meeting, the Industrial Designer will prepare the revised quote, the User Interface Designer will update the sketches with the wedge and name window, and the Marketing Expert will create evaluation criteria based on the survey. Finally, the team confirmed there were no other topics to discuss and concluded the meeting.
predictions.SY0209d: The team reviewed evaluation scores and case details, confirming the wedge design, name tag pocket specifications, and a price of twenty-five euros. They rejected a shoulder strap and assigned Ben to investigate toy safety and request physical samples in blue and lime green. Finally, the project manager reviewed the action items, assigning Priya to do final drawings and Tomasz to write up the evaluation scores.
predictions.SY0304a: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting for the campus parking availability display project and outlined the four-meeting schedule. The team discussed initial ideas, agreeing that the display should show available space counts and color indicators for staff, students, and visitors, while also considering solar power and how signs will detect spaces. They then debated barrier counters versus bay sensors, assigning Marcus to research sensing options, unit costs, and outdoor casings. Finally, the marketing expert agreed to survey campus users, the user interface designer will sketch screen layouts in multiple sizes, and the team decided to focus exclusively on the physical signs rather than an app for now. The project manager concluded the meeting by scheduling the next session for the same time next week and agreed to distribute the meeting minutes and project brief today.
predictions.SY0304b: The project manager reviewed survey demand for readability and app access, and the team selected a large LED display powered by the barrier supply. They decided on barrier counters with a nightly reset, and the project manager agreed to check with estates regarding a central sign. Finally, tasks were assigned for mains checks, the LED layout, and visitor feedback.
predictions.SY0304c: The project manager opened the meeting reviewing the layout, feedback, and power availability across the car parks, while selecting a navy powder-coated casing. Turning to finances, the project manager noted the base cost comes to three hundred ninety pounds per sign leaving ten pounds to spare, though the library car park remains an unknown. Finally, the team agreed to stick with a nightly reset for barrier drift for now and deferred the QR code idea to the end of the project before concluding the call.
predictions.SY0304d: The Project Manager opened the detailed design meeting, noting that estates agreed to cover the library electrics cost. The team agreed on mounting details, finalized cost calculations, discussed counter drift, and reviewed survey requirements. Finally, they assigned remaining action items before closing the meeting.
